question: What document primarily guides the operations of the Nigerian Civil Service?

options.A: The Federal Hospital Management Code
options.B: The National Health Policy Act
options.C: The Civil Service Handbook
options.D: The Nursing and Midwifery Tariff

explanation: The Civil Service Handbook and associated rules regulate the employment and conduct of public servants in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h1)

question: Why must Nigerian nurses working in public facilities understand civil service rules?

options.A: To replace the Nursing and Midwifery Council curriculum
options.B: To navigate employment rights and institutional responsibilities
options.C: To bypass hospital management during emergencies
options.D: To dictate private hospital salary structures nationwide

explanation: Knowledge of these regulations helps nurses understand their rights, obligations, and standards of public administration. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h1)

question: Which body provides the legal backing for nursing practice and licensure in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: Nigerian Medical Association Board
options.D: Civil Service Commission of the Federation

explanation: The NMCN Act authorizes the council to regulate nursing education, practice, and professional discipline in the country. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h2)

question: A nurse who commits an administrative breach of duty faces sanctions from which authority?

options.A: Civil service disciplinary procedures
options.B: Private hospital administrative boards
options.C: International health organization panels
options.D: The National Industrial Court exclusively

explanation: Administrative breaches within public health institutions are handled according to established civil service disciplinary guidelines. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h2)

question: What is the standard duration of the probationary period for newly appointed civil servants in Nigeria?

options.A: Six months
options.B: Two years
options.C: One year
options.D: Five years

explanation: New nursing officers undergo a two-year probation to assess their professional competence and suitability before permanent confirmation. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h3)

question: What requirement must a nurse fulfill before permanent confirmation in the civil service?

options.A: Acquiring a master's degree in public health
options.B: Serving as head of nursing in a facility
options.C: Passing the prescribed civil service examination
options.D: Completing mandatory overseas training programs

explanation: Confirmation of appointment is contingent upon satisfactory job performance and passing the formal civil service confirmation examination. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h3)

question: Which government body monitors public officers to prevent conflicts of interest?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council
options.B: Federal Ministry of Health
options.C: Public Complaints Commission
options.D: Code of Conduct Bureau

explanation: The Code of Conduct Bureau is constitutionally mandated to establish and enforce standards of behavior for public officers. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h4)

question: Why are career nurses in public service restricted from active partisan politics?

options.A: To reduce the total number of government voters
options.B: To prevent them from joining professional associations
options.C: To maintain political neutrality within healthcare institutions
options.D: To ensure they work night shifts without interruption

explanation: Civil service regulations restrict partisan politics to ensure public services are delivered impartially regardless of political affiliations. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h4)

question: What is the standard duration of maternity leave for female officers in the Nigerian civil service?

options.A: 12 weeks
options.B: 24 weeks
options.C: 6 weeks
options.D: 16 weeks

explanation: Federal civil service rules grant female public servants 16 weeks of paid maternity leave. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h5)

question: How is extended sick leave justified for a nurse in public service?

options.A: Presentation of a certified medical report from an approved government hospital
options.B: Approval from the local nursing association executives
options.C: A verbal agreement with the unit nursing officer in charge
options.D: Submitting a personal letter explaining fatigue from work

explanation: Sick leave requires proper medical documentation validated by an authorized government medical board or physician. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h5)

question: What report is regularly used by supervisors to assess a nurse's performance for promotion?

options.A: Patient Satisfaction Survey Log
options.B: Annual Performance Evaluation Report
options.C: Monthly Clinical Audit Summary
options.D: Nursing Council Disciplinary Record

explanation: The APER form is the standard tool used in the civil service to grade employee performance over the year. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h6)

question: What factor besides time spent on a grade level influences a nurse's promotion?

options.A: Completing voluntary community outreach programs
options.B: Securing sponsorship from international donors
options.C: Donating equipment to the hospital ward
options.D: Passing promotional examinations and positive performance reports

explanation: Advancement requires meeting specific exam criteria and maintaining satisfactory evaluations in addition to the mandatory waiting period. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h6)

question: What is the first formal step taken against a civil servant accused of an offense?

options.A: Immediate dismissal from service
options.B: Arrest by security personnel
options.C: Issuing a written query
options.D: Public suspension announcement

explanation: Due process requires that an officer be served a formal written query and given the opportunity to make a representation before disciplinary action. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h7)

question: What channel should a nurse use when seeking redress for perceived administrative injustice?

options.A: Ignoring hospital directives until the issue resolves
options.B: Striking immediately without notifying hospital management
options.C: Publishing complaints on social media platforms
options.D: Hierarchical administrative channels up to the Civil Service Commission

explanation: Grievances must be channeled through established administrative procedures and appeal structures within the civil service. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h7)

question: What are the statutory conditions for retirement in the Nigerian civil service?

options.A: 55 years of age or 30 years of service
options.B: 65 years of age or 40 years of service
options.C: 50 years of age or 20 years of service
options.D: 60 years of age or 35 years of service

explanation: Public servants must retire upon reaching 60 years of chronological age or completing 35 years of active pensionable service, whichever occurs first. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h8)

question: How is the current pension scheme funded for Nigerian civil servants?

options.A: Exclusively through annual federal budget allocations
options.B: By deductions from patient hospital bill payments
options.C: Through private loans secured by the health ministry
options.D: Through monthly contributions by both employer and employee

explanation: The Contributory Pension Scheme requires joint funding contributions from the government employer and the individual worker. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h8)

question: What is the primary funding source for a standard public health agency?

options.A: Direct commercial sales
options.B: International loan interests
options.C: Private corporate donations
options.D: Government budgetary allocations

explanation: Public agencies rely directly on government budgets to fund their administrative and regulatory functions. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h1)

question: Why does a public corporation have a distinct legal personality compared to a basic government department?

options.A: To avoid paying taxes on employee salaries
options.B: To hold property and sue in its own name
options.C: To bypass all national labor laws
options.D: To operate completely free from any government oversight

explanation: A distinct corporate personality allows these entities to handle assets, enter contracts, and engage in legal processes independently. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h1)

question: Which Nigerian agency is directly responsible for regulating nursing education and practice?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: Federal Ministry of Health
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration

explanation: The NMCN holds the statutory mandate to regulate standards for nursing education and professional conduct in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h2)

question: A hospital pharmacy purchases a batch of expired or fake drugs. Which agency investigates this violation?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity
options.B: National Health Insurance Authority
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: NAFDAC regulates and controls the manufacture, distribution, and safety of drugs and medical devices in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h2)

question: What type of accountability involves a public hospital reporting its financial expenditures to a legislative committee?

options.A: Lateral accountability
options.B: Horizontal accountability
options.C: Upward accountability
options.D: Downward accountability

explanation: Reporting to higher supervisory bodies like ministries or parliaments constitutes upward accountability. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h3)

question: How does downward accountability primarily manifest in a public health institution?

options.A: Submitting annual tax returns to the internal revenue service
options.B: Undergoing internal audits by the hospital finance department
options.C: Responsiveness to community needs and patient safety standards
options.D: Meeting federal revenue targets set by the legislature

explanation: Downward accountability focuses on the clients and communities who receive direct care from the health institution. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h3)

question: What is a frequent misconception regarding legal liability among nurse administrators in public institutions?

options.A: Government employment completely shields them from personal liability for gross negligence
options.B: Their licensing council has no jurisdiction over administrative duties
options.C: They are personally responsible for all national health policy failures
options.D: They cannot be sued unless they own shares in the hospital

explanation: Public service does not grant immunity from personal liability resulting from criminal acts or gross professional negligence. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h4)

question: A nurse manager knowingly assigns an untrained auxiliary worker to administer intravenous chemotherapy due to severe staff shortages. What primary professional risk does this present?

options.A: Immunity from legal action due to resource scarcity
options.B: Severe legal liability and professional misconduct charges
options.C: Immediate promotion for solving a staffing crisis
options.D: Exemption from hospital disciplinary committee reviews

explanation: Assigning unqualified personnel to complex tasks violates safety standards and exposes the administrator to severe disciplinary and legal action. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical challenge faced by public health institutions in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive private sector financial surplus
options.B: Chronic infrastructural underfunding
options.C: Migration of skilled healthcare personnel
options.D: Bureaucratic procurement delays

explanation: Public institutions generally suffer from funding deficits rather than having an excess of private financial surplus. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h5)

question: How does bureaucratic red tape negatively impact daily nursing care in public hospitals?

options.A: By ensuring all administrative complaints are resolved instantly
options.B: By speeding up the recruitment of qualified nurse specialists
options.C: By delaying the procurement of emergency medications and supplies
options.D: By removing the need for inter-departmental communication

explanation: Rigid administrative procedures and slow approvals frequently stall access to essential consumables required for patient care. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h5)

question: What does public accountability primarily require a nurse manager to do?

options.A: Increase the monthly budget of the facility
options.B: Answer for resource usage and clinical outcomes
options.C: Handle disciplinary cases among junior doctors
options.D: Purchase private equipment for the hospital ward

explanation: Public accountability centers on stewardship and answering to stakeholders for operational decisions, resource allocation, and patient care outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h1)

question: A nurse leader fails to manage ward supplies well, leading to medicine shortages. Which concept has this leader violated?

options.A: Physician delegation
options.B: Medical confidentiality
options.C: Clinical autonomy
options.D: Public accountability

explanation: Wasting or mismanaging public resources entrusted to a nurse manager violates the core principles of public accountability. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h1)

question: Which body is empowered by an Act to regulate nursing practice and training in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Health
options.B: Nigerian Medical Association
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: West African Health Organization

explanation: The NMCN derives its legal mandate from an Act of Parliament to regulate all tiers of nursing education and clinical practice in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h2)

question: Why must a public health nurse leader understand civil service rules and health acts?

options.A: To bypass financial auditing processes completely
options.B: To prescribe medications independently to patients
options.C: To replace the hospital chief medical director
options.D: To ensure administrative decisions stay within legal boundaries

explanation: Compliance with civil service rules and health acts protects the administrator and the health institution from legal liabilities and malpractice. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of checks and balances in a public hospital?

options.A: Eliminating the need for external government oversight
options.B: Slowing down emergency care delivery in the wards
options.C: Preventing any single individual from holding absolute power
options.D: Ensuring doctors earn higher salaries than nurses

explanation: Distributing power and duties among different offices prevents abuse, corruption, and unilateral decision-making. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h3)

question: A nurse unit manager wants to purchase new oxygen cylinders. Following checks and balances, who should verify the delivery before payment?

options.A: The same nurse manager who ordered them
options.B: The external police force in the state
options.C: An independent store officer or internal audit unit
options.D: Patients admitted to the accident and emergency ward

explanation: Separating the ordering function from the verification and payment functions ensures proper internal control and transparency. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h3)

question: Funds generated directly by a public health facility through services are referred to as what?

options.A: Personal staff contributions
options.B: Donor community grants
options.C: Internally generated revenue
options.D: Federal capital subvention

explanation: Internally generated revenue (IGR) represents fees and collections made directly by the hospital from patient services and other commercial ventures. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h4)

question: Which activity is a direct violation of financial integrity in nursing administration?

options.A: Consulting staff before drafting the annual ward budget
options.B: Padding budget estimates to siphon public funds
options.C: Requesting more syringes for an overcrowded emergency ward
options.D: Reporting damaged equipment to the maintenance unit

explanation: Budget padding to misappropriate public funds directly breaches financial integrity and anti-corruption regulations. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h4)

question: Who conducts external financial audits for public institutions in Nigeria?

options.A: The local nurses' trade union
options.B: The head pharmacist of the facility
options.C: The hospital's chief nursing officer
options.D: The Office of the Auditor-General

explanation: External audits are legally mandated to be carried out by independent supreme audit institutions like the Auditor-General's office. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h5)

question: Why are routine internal audits important in a public health facility?

options.A: To increase the prices of drugs at the hospital pharmacy
options.B: To replace the need for professional nursing supervision
options.C: To punish nurses who refuse to work night shifts
options.D: To catch financial errors and discrepancies early before external audits

explanation: Internal audits act as an early warning system to correct financial mistakes and prevent fraud before statutory external auditors review the books. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h5)

question: What is a primary ethical duty of a nurse leader facing institutional wrongdoing?

options.A: Blaming junior nursing students for the mistake
options.B: Reporting the wrongdoing and protecting whistleblowers
options.C: Ignoring the incident to maintain peace among staff
options.D: Resigning immediately without notifying authorities

explanation: Ethical nursing leadership demands professional courage to expose corruption and safeguard those who report malpractice. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h6)

question: A nurse manager assigns choice shifts only to personal friends while ignoring equitable rostering. This violates which professional value?

options.A: Emergency triage protocols
options.B: Patient confidentiality rules
options.C: Informed consent guidelines
options.D: Fairness and professional equity

explanation: Showing bias in duty rostering violates the ethical standard of fairness and destroys team morale in the workplace. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h6)

question: A patient is asked to pay a bribe before receiving emergency treatment in a public clinic. What mechanism should address this grievance?

options.A: Ignoring the complaint to protect the hospital's image
options.B: A functional hospital complaint desk and anti-corruption unit
options.C: Public protests outside the ministry of works
options.D: Immediate dismissal of all nursing staff on duty

explanation: Institutions require structured grievance redress channels like complaint desks and anti-corruption units to investigate and resolve extortion claims. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common manifestation of maladministration in public hospitals?

options.A: Extortion of informal fees from vulnerable patients
options.B: Chronic staff absenteeism from assigned clinical wards
options.C: Prompt and equitable delivery of patient care to all
options.D: Diversion of government-supplied drugs to private chemist shops

explanation: Prompt and equitable care represents good governance and high-quality administration, not maladministration. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h7)

question: What is the legal status of most nurses working in hospitals?

options.A: Independent contractor
options.B: Sole proprietor
options.C: Hospital employee
options.D: Corporate shareholder

explanation: Nurses who work on a salary inside a healthcare facility are considered employees, which connects their duties directly to the hospital. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h1)

question: Why does a nurse's employment status matter if a professional mistake happens?

options.A: It decides staff quarters allocation.
options.B: It dictates the post-lawsuit salary scale.
options.C: It determines who shares financial and legal responsibility for the mistake.
options.D: It changes the registered professional title.

explanation: Whether a nurse is an employee or an independent contractor affects how legal blame and damages are shared between the nurse and the hospital. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h1)

question: Which organization regulates nursing education and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Health
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the official body set up to regulate and control nursing practice across the country. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h2)

question: What happens legally when a nurse performs procedures outside their allowed scope of practice?

options.A: Loss of legal protection and exposure to disciplinary action
options.B: Automatic promotion
options.C: Immediate transfer with higher pay
options.D: Exemption from shift duties

explanation: Going beyond authorized practice boundaries removes insurance cover and brings legal penalties from the courts and the regulatory council. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h2)

question: What is the first thing a plaintiff must prove in a civil lawsuit for nursing negligence?

options.A: Written confession
options.B: Failure of hospital equipment
options.C: Intentional harm
options.D: Existence of a duty of care

explanation: A legal duty must first exist between the healthcare provider and the patient before any failure in care can be claimed. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h3)

question: A nurse forgets to check a patient's ID band, gives the wrong blood type, and causes a severe reaction. What legal concept applies here?

options.A: Professional malpractice and negligence
options.B: Corporate negligence
options.C: Informed refusal
options.D: Lawful delegation

explanation: Failing to follow basic safety checks that lead to patient harm is considered a breach of the standard of care, which is negligence. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h3)

question: What does the legal phrase respondeat superior mean in healthcare law?

options.A: Patient above all else
options.B: Let the master answer
options.C: First do no harm
options.D: Always secure written consent

explanation: Respondeat superior means the employer takes legal responsibility for the workplace negligence of employees. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h4)

question: When is a hospital most likely to be held responsible for a nurse's medication error?

options.A: When the error happened while the nurse was doing routine ward duties on shift
options.B: When the nurse made the error while off duty visiting relatives
options.C: When the nurse ignored all hospital guidelines
options.D: When the nurse was running a private clinic

explanation: The employer shares responsibility only when the wrongful act happens during the active execution of normal job duties. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is a direct example of corporate negligence by a hospital?

options.A: A single nurse miscalculating a drug dose
options.B: A visitor slipping on a dry floor
options.C: Employing nurses who lack valid professional licenses
options.D: A patient refusing oral medications

explanation: Failing to check credentials and hiring unqualified staff is a direct institutional failure by the hospital management. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h5)

question: How does corporate negligence differ from vicarious liability?

options.A: Corporate negligence involves the hospital's direct failure, while vicarious liability transfers blame from an employee.
options.B: Corporate negligence only applies to private clinics.
options.C: Corporate negligence protects nurses from discipline.
options.D: Vicarious liability requires criminal intent.

explanation: Corporate negligence targets the institution's own failure, whereas vicarious liability shifts blame upward from the worker to the boss. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h5)

question: What legal charge may apply if a nurse performs a procedure on a conscious adult without valid consent?

options.A: Slander
options.B: Defamation
options.C: Breach of contract
options.D: Battery

explanation: Touching a patient without lawful permission or valid consent is legally classified as battery in civil law. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h6)

question: When is a nurse legally allowed to bypass informed consent?

options.A: During emergencies where an unconscious patient needs immediate life-saving care
options.B: When the nurse feels the treatment will help
options.C: When the patient is from a low-income background
options.D: Whenever the doctor is too busy to explain

explanation: Implied consent applies in real emergencies when immediate care is needed to save a life or prevent permanent harm. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h6)

question: What is the main legal purpose of keeping accurate and prompt nursing documentation?

options.A: It serves as primary legal evidence of the care provided.
options.B: It replaces verbal handovers.
options.C: It exempts the nurse from signing attendance registers.
options.D: It guarantees an allowance increase.

explanation: Medical records are legally admissible documents used to prove what care was actually delivered to a patient. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h7)

question: Which practice helps protect a nurse from financial ruin if a malpractice lawsuit is filed?

options.A: Maintaining active professional indemnity insurance
options.B: Delegating all documentation to students
options.C: Refusing to sign incident reports
options.D: Destroying patient charts after a bad outcome

explanation: Indemnity insurance gives financial protection against legal damages awarded in professional negligence cases. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h7)

question: What do clients' rights primarily ensure for individuals receiving medical care?

options.A: Immediate discharge upon demand
options.B: Treatment with dignity and respect
options.C: Free medical care in all hospitals
options.D: Complete exemption from hospital rules

explanation: Clients' rights guarantee that patients receive respectful and dignified treatment during their healthcare interactions. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h1)

question: Why is recognizing patient rights important in clinical practice?

options.A: It eliminates the need for written medical records
options.B: It removes all legal responsibilities from nurses
options.C: It guarantees financial profit for the hospital
options.D: It balances power between workers and patients

explanation: Acknowledging these rights reduces the traditional power imbalance between healthcare providers and patients. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h1)

question: Which ethical principle refers to the duty of doing no harm to the patient?

options.A: Justice
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Non-maleficence
options.D: Beneficence

explanation: Non-maleficence specifically mandates that healthcare providers avoid causing harm to their patients. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h2)

question: A nurse who advocates for equal treatment for all ward patients regardless of wealth is practicing what?

options.A: Veracity
options.B: Beneficence
options.C: Justice
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Justice involves treating all individuals fairly and distributing healthcare resources equitably. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h2)

question: What does the right to information guarantee a healthcare client?

options.A: Full control over hospital administration
options.B: Access to the personal salaries of doctors
options.C: Copies of the hospital annual financial report
options.D: Details about diagnosis and treatment options

explanation: Patients have the right to clear information concerning their medical condition, treatment plans, and expected outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h3)

question: A patient complains about poor nursing service through official hospital channels. This action exercises which specific right?

options.A: The right to free medical supplies
options.B: The right to modify hospital policies directly
options.C: The right to immediate discharge against medical advice
options.D: The right to voice complaints and receive redress

explanation: Clients have a recognized right to express dissatisfaction and seek solutions through appropriate grievance mechanisms. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h3)

question: Who holds the primary responsibility for explaining a surgical procedure to obtain informed consent?

options.A: The hospital accountant
options.B: The attending physician
options.C: The security personnel
options.D: The ward cleaner

explanation: The doctor performing the procedure is legally responsible for explaining risks, benefits, and securing informed consent. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h4)

question: A competent adult patient refuses a blood transfusion due to personal beliefs. What is the correct nursing action?

options.A: Force the patient to sign a consent form
options.B: Administer the blood while the patient sleeps
options.C: Call security to restrain the patient
options.D: Respect the refusal and inform the doctor

explanation: Competent adults possess the legal right to refuse any medical treatment, requiring the nurse to respect autonomy and report to the physician. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h4)

question: Which situation represents a legal exception to maintaining client confidentiality?

options.A: Sharing patient gossip with a colleague at lunch
options.B: Posting a patient's recovery progress online
options.C: Discussing clinical cases with curious neighbors
options.D: Reporting suspected child abuse to authorities

explanation: Mandatory reporting laws require nurses to breach confidentiality in specific public safety instances like child abuse. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary difference between privacy and confidentiality in nursing?

options.A: Privacy relates to money, confidentiality relates to health
options.B: Privacy concerns physical access, confidentiality concerns shared information
options.C: Privacy only applies to doctors, confidentiality only applies to nurses
options.D: Privacy is optional, confidentiality is strictly mandatory

explanation: Privacy protects the patient's body and personal space, while confidentiality protects the data they share. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h5)

question: What does the legal term liability mean in healthcare practice?

options.A: Ownership of hospital equipment
options.B: Responsibility for one's actions or omissions
options.C: Immunity from all court lawsuits
options.D: The right to refuse going to work

explanation: Liability is the legal accountability a healthcare provider holds for the care they deliver or fail to deliver. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h6)

question: Why is a nurse held accountable for following an obviously dangerous medical prescription?

options.A: Doctors have no legal standing in a court of law
options.B: Nurses are legally superior to medical doctors
options.C: Hospital management pays all fines for nurses
options.D: Nurses have an independent duty to protect patients from harm

explanation: Professional accountability requires nurses to question unsafe orders rather than blindly execute them. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h6)

question: What is the term for a civil wrong committed against a person or property?

options.A: Contract
options.B: Tort
options.C: Statute
options.D: Felony

explanation: A tort is a civil wrong that causes injury or harm, serving as the basis for legal lawsuits in healthcare. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h7)

question: Which element must be proven alongside breach of duty for a malpractice suit to succeed?

options.A: The patient failed to pay their medical bills
options.B: Actual injury or damages occurred to the patient
options.C: The nurse had a personal disagreement with the doctor
options.D: The hospital was operating at a financial loss

explanation: Damages are a mandatory element of a malpractice claim; without actual harm, a suit cannot be sustained. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h7)

question: What is a primary rule regarding clinical documentation in risk management?

options.A: If it was not charted, legally it was not done
options.B: Only document abnormal lab results in pencil
options.C: Write patient reports at the end of the week
options.D: Chart all medications twenty-four hours in advance

explanation: Courts rely heavily on medical records as legal proof of care; unrecorded care is treated as unperformed care. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h8)

question: How does maintaining open communication with patients help prevent legal liabilities?

options.A: It prevents patients from developing any illnesses
options.B: It eliminates the need for written consent forms
options.C: It reduces misunderstandings and builds trust
options.D: It waives the patient's right to sue the hospital

explanation: Transparent communication fosters trust and reduces grievances when complications arise during treatment. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h8)

question: What does the legal term 'respondeat superior' mean?

options.A: Above all, do no harm
options.B: Let the master answer
options.C: To err is human
options.D: The thing speaks for itself

explanation: Respondeat superior translates to let the master answer, which means the employer is held responsible for the employee's actions. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h1)

question: Why do injured patients often sue the hospital instead of just the nurse?

options.A: Hospitals have more money to pay settlements
options.B: State laws forbid suing hospital staff
options.C: Hospitals make patients sign agreements
options.D: Nurses cannot be sued in court

explanation: Injured plaintiffs often target employers because organizations have the financial resources to cover large damage awards. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h1)

question: What type of relationship must exist between a nurse and a hospital for vicarious liability to apply?

options.A: Business partners
options.B: Employer and employee
options.C: Regulator and licensee
options.D: Vendor and consumer

explanation: Vicarious liability requires a formal employment relationship so the institution can be held accountable for worker negligence. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h2)

question: A nurse intentionally harms someone during a personal fight outside of work. Who is mainly responsible?

options.A: The hospital employer
options.B: The medical director
options.C: The shift supervisor
options.D: The nurse individually

explanation: Actions outside the scope of employment and caused by personal malice do not make the employer liable under respondeat superior. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h2)

question: What does personal liability mean for a professional nurse?

options.A: Paying insurance for the whole ward
options.B: Representing the hospital in court
options.C: Answering for one's own clinical mistakes
options.D: Taking blame for broken hospital equipment

explanation: Personal liability means each nurse must take direct responsibility for their own professional errors and omissions. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h3)

question: How is personal liability different from vicarious liability?

options.A: Personal liability needs no proof of injury.
options.B: Vicarious liability revokes licenses.
options.C: Personal liability only applies to doctors.
options.D: Personal liability targets the worker, while vicarious liability targets the employer.

explanation: The main difference is who takes the blame for the mistake: the actual worker or the supervising organization. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h3)

question: Why are hospitals usually not held liable for independent contractors?

options.A: State laws ban lawsuits involving contractors.
options.B: The hospital does not control their daily work methods.
options.C: Contractors always carry personal insurance.
options.D: Contractors are not allowed to make mistakes.

explanation: Because the facility lacks direct control over how independent contractors do their jobs, the institution is usually shielded from liability. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h4)

question: A patient assumes an agency nurse works for the hospital and sues the facility over a drug error. What legal concept applies here?

options.A: Statute of limitations
options.B: Ostensible agency
options.C: Charitable immunity
options.D: Res ipsa loquitur

explanation: Ostensible agency applies when a patient reasonably believes a contract worker is a regular employee of the facility. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h4)

question: What is it called when a hospital hires a nurse without checking their license or background?

options.A: Vicarious delegation
options.B: Ostensible contracting
options.C: Corporate malpractice
options.D: Negligent credentialing

explanation: Failing to properly screen, verify, or credential nursing staff is known as negligent credentialing by administration. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h5)

question: When is a nurse manager directly liable for a staff member's mistake?

options.A: If the manager was off duty during the incident
options.B: When the manager assigned an unqualified nurse to a high-risk unit
options.C: Whenever any nurse on duty makes a charting error
options.D: Because managers are always vicariously liable

explanation: Managers can be held liable for their own administrative errors, such as poor task assignment or weak supervision. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h5)

question: What is the main goal of risk management regarding vicarious liability?

options.A: Preventing patient harm and reducing legal risks
options.B: Hiding medical errors from regulators
options.C: Removing the need for liability insurance
options.D: Shifting all fines onto junior nurses

explanation: Risk management aims to protect patient health outcomes while keeping the organization safe from legal claims. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h6)

question: Which administrative tool ensures staff only perform tasks allowed by their training and license?

options.A: Public grievance boards
options.B: Monthly salary reviews
options.C: Detailed job descriptions
options.D: Union membership dues

explanation: Clear job descriptions set boundaries so staff members work safely within their legal scope of practice. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h6)

question: What makes professional malpractice different from general negligence?

options.A: Malpractice only happens during surgeries in a hospital.
options.B: Malpractice involves breaking a professional standard of care.
options.C: General negligence has heavier criminal punishments.
options.D: General negligence requires a bad intention from the worker.

explanation: Malpractice specifically requires breaking the recognized standard expected from a licensed professional, unlike general negligence which applies to ordinary people. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h1)

question: An off-duty nurse does not help someone who collapsed on the street. Is this professional malpractice?

options.A: No, because there was no nurse-patient relationship.
options.B: Yes, because nurses are always on duty everywhere.
options.C: No, unless the nurse caused the person to collapse.
options.D: Yes, not helping outside the hospital is a licensing crime.

explanation: Professional malpractice requires a duty of care, which only exists when a professional relationship has been established between the nurse and the patient. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h1)

question: A patient proves a nurse made a drug error, but suffered no actual harm. Which part of malpractice is missing?

options.A: Causation
options.B: Breach
options.C: Damages
options.D: Duty

explanation: Damages refer to actual injury or loss suffered by the patient. Without injury, a malpractice claim cannot succeed even if a mistake happened. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h2)

question: Proving that a nurse's careless action directly caused a patient's complication establishes which legal element?

options.A: Causation
options.B: Consent
options.C: Capacity
options.D: Damages

explanation: Causation links the nurse's specific breach of duty directly to the negative outcome experienced by the patient. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h2)

question: Which situation is most likely to lead to an immediate negligence claim?

options.A: Asking a student nurse to make an unassisted bed
options.B: Arriving ten minutes late for morning handover
options.C: Leaving out a patient's food preference on the chart
options.D: Giving the wrong blood type because identity checks were skipped

explanation: Skipping vital safety checks like patient identification during high-risk procedures like blood transfusions directly breaches the standard of care and causes severe harm. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h3)

question: Why is it dangerous to fail to report worsening vital signs to a doctor?

options.A: It causes confusion during the verbal shift report.
options.B: It delays critical care and worsens patient outcomes.
options.C: It automatically revokes the nursing license.
options.D: It breaks hospital financial rules on patient turnover.

explanation: Failing to communicate clinical changes prevents timely medical intervention, which directly contributes to patient injury or death. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h3)

question: Which body in Nigeria can suspend or revoke a nurse's license for malpractice?

options.A: Nigerian Medical Association
options.B: Federal Ministry of Health
options.C: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body responsible for licensing, discipline, and maintaining professional standards for nurses in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h4)

question: Why might a nurse face both a civil lawsuit and disciplinary action from the council?

options.A: The hospital forces the council to investigate all civil cases.
options.B: Criminal courts automatically report every guilty verdict to the health ministry.
options.C: Civil law handles money for damages while the council handles licensing.
options.D: Nigerian law requires two trials for any workplace error.

explanation: Civil courts deal with compensating the victim for damages, whereas regulatory bodies like the council protect the public by policing professional conduct and licensure. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h4)

question: What does the statute of limitations defense rely on in a malpractice lawsuit?

options.A: The patient failed to follow the nursing care plan.
options.B: Another worker caused the main injury.
options.C: Hospital equipment broke despite proper maintenance.
options.D: The lawsuit was filed after the legal time limit expired.

explanation: The statute of limitations sets a strict timeframe within which a legal action must be started after an incident occurs. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h5)

question: A patient ignores discharge instructions, removes a wound dressing early, and gets an infection. Which defense applies best?

options.A: Res ipsa loquitur
options.B: Contributory negligence
options.C: Good Samaritan protection
options.D: Statute of limitations

explanation: Contributory negligence applies when the patient's own careless behavior plays a direct role in causing or worsening their injury. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h5)

question: Which practice is the strongest legal defense for a nurse accused of negligence?

options.A: Apologizing immediately to the family after an event
options.B: Clear, accurate, and prompt documentation in the patient chart
options.C: Destroying broken medication vials before filing a report
options.D: Relying on verbal handovers instead of written records

explanation: Medical records written at the time of care provide objective proof and are heavily relied upon in legal proceedings. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h6)

question: What is the main goal of completing an incident report after a medication mistake?

options.A: To give police immediate evidence to arrest the nurse
options.B: To prove to the patient that it was an honest mistake
options.C: To find system flaws and improve future patient safety
options.D: To lower the hospital's annual tax and insurance fees

explanation: Incident reports are internal tools used to analyze errors, find system weaknesses, and prevent future occurrences. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h6)

question: What does the philosophy of management primarily examine?

options.A: Patient disease pathology and drug interactions
options.B: Underlying assumptions and values guiding leadership
options.C: Surgical sterilization techniques and protocols
options.D: The exact daily budget of a hospital ward

explanation: Management philosophy looks at the fundamental beliefs and values that shape how leaders direct their organizations. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why must a nurse manager examine personal leadership beliefs?

options.A: To ensure daily ward actions are purposeful rather than reactive
options.B: To fulfill mandatory government clinical nursing hours
options.C: To diagnose complex tropical medical conditions alone
options.D: To calculate exact patient medication dosages safely

explanation: Examining core beliefs helps leaders move past random reactions and guide their teams with clear purpose. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h1)

question: The classical management school primarily focused on which factor?

options.A: Employee psychological counseling
options.B: Efficiency and mechanical output
options.C: Flexible, situational leadership
options.D: External environmental adaptation

explanation: Classical theorists concentrated on standardization, division of labor, and maximizing physical productivity. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the main premise of the contingency management approach?

options.A: Workers are solely motivated by financial incentives
options.B: Organizations operate completely isolated from society
options.C: The best leadership style depends on the specific situation
options.D: Strict hierarchy solves every organizational problem

explanation: Contingency theory rejects one-size-fits-all solutions, stating that the right method changes based on context. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h2)

question: Utilitarianism evaluates management decisions based on what outcome?

options.A: Personal financial profit for directors
options.B: Individual employee career promotion
options.C: Strict adherence to written legal codes
options.D: The greatest good for the greatest number

explanation: Utilitarian philosophy measures the morality of an action by its overall benefit to the majority. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h3)

question: A nurse manager using virtue ethics will focus primarily on which attribute?

options.A: Enforcing rigid hospital security protocols
options.B: Developing personal moral character and compassion
options.C: Meeting strict government patient turnover quotas
options.D: Calculating exact cost-benefit ratios for supplies

explanation: Virtue ethics emphasizes the internal moral traits and character of the decision-maker. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h3)

question: Corporate social responsibility requires leaders to balance economic gains with what factor?

options.A: The welfare of the broader community
options.B: Aggressive competitor market share
options.C: Immediate personal executive bonuses
options.D: Maximum daily product pricing limits

explanation: Social responsibility mandates that organizational leaders consider societal impact alongside financial profit. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h4)

question: Ethical management in a healthcare facility directly leads to which positive outcome?

options.A: Guaranteed immunity from medical malpractice suits
options.B: Automatic promotion of all junior nursing staff
options.C: Higher institutional trust and reduced staff burnout
options.D: Elimination of all operational hospital expenses

explanation: Upholding strong ethical values fosters trust and supports staff well-being in high-stress environments. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h4)

question: Theory X assumes which of the following about workers?

options.A: They prefer total autonomy over financial pay
options.B: They are fully self-motivated and creative
options.C: They naturally seek responsibility and growth
options.D: They are lazy and require close supervision

explanation: Theory X holds a pessimistic view of human nature, presuming workers dislike labor and need strict control. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h5)

question: A head nurse gives experienced staff autonomy and encourages professional growth. Which theory is being applied?

options.A: Theory X
options.B: Classical Scientific
options.C: Theory Y
options.D: Utilitarianism

explanation: Trusting staff and fostering autonomy aligns with Theory Y assumptions regarding human motivation. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary effect of a punitive workplace culture?

options.A: Operational efficiency reaches maximum levels
options.B: Communication between departments improves
options.C: Staff eagerly report every minor mistake
options.D: Errors are hidden out of fear of punishment

explanation: When punishment is guaranteed for mistakes, employees conceal errors rather than reporting them for learning. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h6)

question: How does a just culture influence clinical error management?

options.A: It encourages open reporting and systemic learning
options.B: It mandates immediate dismissal for any oversight
options.C: It completely eliminates all human clinical mistakes
options.D: It shifts all legal blame entirely to the patient

explanation: A just culture separates honest mistakes from reckless behavior, promoting transparency and safety improvement. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h6)

question: Where does applying management philosophy directly impact nursing practice?

options.A: In performing major surgical procedures independently
options.B: In shift rostering, conflict resolution, and resource advocacy
options.C: In writing national health legislation and laws
options.D: In manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs and vaccines

explanation: Ward leaders use management philosophy practically when organizing staff duties and handling daily conflicts. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h7)

question: A nurse supervisor adopts a humanistic leadership philosophy. What is the most likely result for the ward staff?

options.A: Shorter patient hospital stays across all diagnoses
options.B: Improved job retention and better patient care standards
options.C: Elimination of all mandatory nursing documentation
options.D: Decreased overall hospital financial expenditures

explanation: Humanistic leadership values staff well-being, which directly improves retention and care quality. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of an organisational structure in a hospital?

options.A: Defines reporting lines and communication channels
options.B: Sets the clinical guidelines for bedside care
options.C: Calculates the staffing ratios for night shifts
options.D: Determines the exact monthly budget for supplies

explanation: An organisational structure outlines formal authority, reporting hierarchies, and official communication pathways within an institution. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h1)

question: Why is having a clear organisational structure important for patient safety?

options.A: It eliminates the need for shift handovers between nursing teams
options.B: It guarantees that nurses receive higher monthly salaries
options.C: It prevents confusion and clinical errors by clarifying responsibilities
options.D: It completely removes the authority of the chief medical director

explanation: Clear role boundaries and reporting lines ensure accountability, preventing gaps in patient care that could lead to clinical errors. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h1)

question: What do we call the number of subordinates that a single manager can effectively direct?

options.A: Span of control
options.B: Work specialisation
options.C: Chain of command
options.D: Centralisation limit

explanation: Span of control refers to the number of workers or subordinates reporting directly to a specific manager. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h2)

question: In hospital management, what is a key result of decentralisation?

options.A: Work specialisation is completely eliminated across all departments
options.B: Communication channels become strictly limited to written memos
options.C: Frontline nurse managers make decisions closer to the point of care
options.D: All operational choices require direct approval from the board chair

explanation: Decentralisation pushes decision-making authority down to lower-level managers who deal with daily operational realities. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h2)

question: How are employees grouped in a functional organisational structure?

options.A: Similar professional skills and specialized tasks
options.B: Temporary project assignments and short-term goals
options.C: Random assignment during shift handovers
options.D: Geographical location of the healthcare facility

explanation: Functional structures organise personnel according to their specific professional functions, such as nursing, finance, or laboratory services. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is a common disadvantage of a strictly functional organisational design?

options.A: Excessive duplication of equipment and support staff units
options.B: Creation of rigid departmental silos that hinder communication
options.C: Complete absence of any formal chain of command
options.D: Unclear reporting lines between nurses and ward managers

explanation: Functional departments often focus inward on their own goals, creating barriers that isolate them from other units. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is a key feature of a matrix organisational structure?

options.A: A strict single-line chain of command from top to bottom
options.B: The complete absence of any designated managers or leaders
options.C: Absolute centralisation of all decisions at the executive level
options.D: Dual reporting relationships to functional and project managers

explanation: Employees in a matrix structure report to two different supervisors, typically a functional head and a project or programme manager. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h4)

question: What is the main advantage of using a team-based structure in a hospital?

options.A: Elimination of the need for any written nursing documentation
options.B: Strict adherence to traditional military command lines
options.C: Lower salary expenditures across all clinical departments
options.D: Enhanced multidisciplinary collaboration to solve complex patient problems

explanation: Team-based designs bring diverse experts together, breaking down silos to improve patient-centred care delivery. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which feature is most typical of a mechanistic organisational structure?

options.A: Fluid roles and extensive cross-functional teamwork
options.B: Minimal supervision and low task specialisation
options.C: High centralisation and rigid formalisation of rules
options.D: Wide spans of control and decentralised authority

explanation: Mechanistic structures rely on strict rules, high centralisation, and tight bureaucratic control. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why is an organic structure better suited for an emergency department than a mechanistic one?

options.A: Organic designs completely eliminate the need for shift reports
options.B: Unpredictable clinical crises require rapid, flexible decision-making
options.C: Emergency staff prefer working without any written protocols
options.D: Mechanistic structures are illegal in acute care hospitals

explanation: Organic structures provide the adaptability needed in fast-paced, unpredictable environments where rigid rules slow down critical responses. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h5)

question: How do strategy and organisational structure relate to one another?

options.A: Budget constraints dictate strategy without regard for structure
options.B: Strategy changes automatically whenever a new manager is hired
options.C: Organisational design has no impact on institutional goals
options.D: Structure must follow and support the chosen strategy

explanation: An institution's structural design must align with and enable its overarching strategic objectives. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h6)

question: How does an uncertain work environment usually affect organisational design?

options.A: Uncertain environments push institutions toward more organic designs
options.B: Environmental changes have no bearing on how hospital wards are run
options.C: High uncertainty forces hospitals to abandon all departmentalisation
options.D: Unstable conditions require stricter mechanistic rules and centralisation

explanation: Uncertainty demands flexibility and decentralisation, steering leaders toward organic structures that can adapt quickly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h6)

question: What main balance must nurse managers maintain within an organisational structure?

options.A: Balancing medical doctor schedules with hospital cleaning rosters
options.B: Balancing administrative control with professional clinical autonomy
options.C: Balancing night shift allowances with annual leave requests
options.D: Balancing pharmacy budgets with laboratory supply inventories

explanation: Nurse leaders must respect institutional hierarchies while supporting the independent clinical judgment required in nursing practice. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h7)

question: A hospital ward has communication delays and missed reports due to too many management layers. What is the best structural fix?

options.A: Flattens the hierarchy and decentralises decision-making authority
options.B: Converts the entire hospital into a strictly mechanistic design
options.C: Adds more middle-management oversight positions to enforce rules
options.D: Centralises all reporting directly through the chief executive officer

explanation: Removing bureaucratic layers and decentralising authority shortens communication lines and speeds up problem resolution. [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of the staffing function in healthcare management?

options.B: Minimizing the promotion of senior nursing officers
options.C: Increasing the number of administrative meetings daily

question: How does proper staffing directly influence clinical outcomes in a hospital?

options.B: It stops patients from getting admitted on weekends
options.C: It guarantees automatic salary increases for all workers
options.D: It lowers the frequency of adverse patient safety events

explanation: Adequate nurse staffing reduces errors and improves overall patient safety and recovery rates. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h1)

question: What factor is most critical when calculating patient acuity for staffing?

options.B: The brand of medication prescribed by the doctor
options.C: The severity of illness and care complexity
options.D: The distance of the patient from the nurses' station

question: Why do nurse managers monitor staff turnover rates during workforce planning?

options.A: To calculate the exact electricity consumption of wards
options.B: To predict future vacancies and plan recruitment drives
options.C: To reduce the number of visiting doctors in the hospital
options.D: To decide which nurses deserve a formal warning query

explanation: Tracking turnover helps managers anticipate when positions will become vacant so replacements can be planned. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h2)

question: What document must every registered nurse present during employment screening in Nigeria?

options.A: A personal letter of recommendation from a politician
options.B: Receipt for hospital car park access
options.C: Proof of membership in a social club
options.D: Current practicing license from the NMCN

question: What is the main difference between recruitment and selection in staffing?

options.A: Recruitment only applies to auxiliary staff members

options.C: Recruitment attracts applicants, while selection chooses the best candidate

question: What is the primary role of a preceptor during a new nurse's orientation?

options.A: Handling the administrative payroll and tax deductions
options.B: Deciding when the hospital canteen should open
options.C: Evaluating the hospital building maintenance schedules
options.D: Providing guidance, supervision, and clinical mentorship

explanation: A preceptor supports and guides the new staff member through daily clinical duties. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h4)

question: Why is structured unit-specific orientation important for newly employed nurses?

options.A: It helps them learn specialized ward routines and equipment quickly
options.B: It replaces the need for an initial nursing qualification
options.C: It allows them to bypass hospital safety regulations
options.D: It ensures they never have to work night shifts

explanation: Different wards have unique equipment and protocols that new staff must learn to practice safely. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h4)

question: What is a major challenge affecting nurse-patient ratios in many Nigerian public hospitals?

options.A: Excessive number of nurses reporting for every single shift
options.B: Shortage of qualified nursing personnel relative to patient load
options.C: Ban on working night shifts by the health ministry
options.D: Mandatory limit of two patients per ward per day

question: Why is maintaining a proper skill mix on every shift important?

options.A: It guarantees that all patients are discharged by midday
options.B: It prevents nurses from taking their mandatory annual leave
options.C: It ensures junior staff have experienced support for complex tasks

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting regular performance appraisals for nurses?

options.A: Providing constructive feedback and identifying areas for growth
options.B: Reducing the number of patients admitted to the ward

question: Why must authority and responsibility be balanced in a nursing unit?
